chat.text:
Hey emu, I also wanted to draw attention to an I-D and LS with 3GPP bumped on the list on AT_IDENTITY fragmentation in EAP-AKA' for PQC:
https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/emu/KWMsc5e1KWfhOT2adIG2fxMb31c/

chat.author: Aritra Banerjee
chat.text:
Andrew Dolan said:

Hey emu, I also wanted to draw attention to an I-D and LS with 3GPP bumped on the list on AT_IDENTITY fragmentation in EAP-AKA' for PQC:
https://mailarchive.ietf.org/arch/msg/emu/KWMsc5e1KWfhOT2adIG2fxMb31c/

I will respond this in the WG list later. The EAP-AKA' PQC fragmentation defined in draft-ietf-emu-pqc-eapaka-02 is generic and can be used for any attribute.

chat.author: Andrew Dolan
chat.text:
Thanks Aritra. That's my understanding and the I-D in question leverages that generic fragmentation:

This document updates EAP-AKA’ (RFC 9048) by defining the use of the AT_FRAGMENT mechanism, as defined in I-D.ietf-emu-pqc-eapaka, for fragmentation of the AT_IDENTITY attribute.

chat.author: Heikki Vatiainen
chat.text: My support is for generic fragmentation.

chat.author: Alan DeKok
chat.text: @heikki - I agree. I'm not sure that it's always possible,.  But a generic solution is preferred to a method-specific one

chat.text: A note: eapoL_test supports EAP-PSK. For interoperability testing, you may want to consider adding support in wpa_supplicant for interoperability testing.

chat.text: @alan It seems the two fragmentation needs with EAP-AKA' extensions can use the same fragmentation method. One option might be to define it in one document and then point to it from those documents that can use it.

chat.author: Göran Selander
chat.text: What regulation are requiring you to change from AES with 128 bits?

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text:
I appreciate the desire to move to AES-256 here.  Most quantum-safe advice say to double your AES keysize.  
What I heard is that EAP-AKA is used today for municipal metering systems, traffic light, etc..

chat.author: Göran Selander
chat.text: Michael: I'm not aware of recommendations of doubling AES key size, do you have a reference?

chat.author: Michael Le Clerc
chat.text: ENISA ==> 192 bits or more

chat.author: Michael Richardson
chat.text: Is it possible for EAP-AKA' enabled SIMs to continue to support EAP-AKA (128-bit), but just truncating?

chat.author: Alan DeKok
chat.text: @mcr this is EAP-PSK, tho.  EAP-AKA is much more widely used

chat.author: Heikki Vatiainen
chat.text: @Emmanuel I'm not Michael but I'd say the EAP-PSK and EAP-AKA and other SIM based EAPs, are not related (other than being EAP methods)

chat.author: Matt G1
chat.text:
@Michael - here's the IETF liaison statement discussing AES (towards the end)
https://datatracker.ietf.org/liaison/1942/
AES-128 is L1 in PQ terms. If there is a use case for L5 (AES-256) then sure I can understand the protocol needs updating. 
I'm not aware of any regulation (outside if CNSA2.0) that mandates L5.

chat.author: Göran Selander
chat.text: Thanks Matt, I was looking for that LS.

chat.author: Michael Le Clerc
chat.text:
@Matt
I agree that AES-128 is still an agreed cryptogrpahic, but perhaps not to protect from "store now, decrypt later" threat. To be discussed.
